Toronto Building Permits: Processing Time & Volume Analysis

Source: README.md, prnjl204/toronto-building-permits

Executive Summary

  • Permit application volume has nearly quadrupled since 2010 (5,220 → 20,549 in 2025), with a sharp acceleration since 2021 — the city's permitting system is under growing load.
  • Median approval time is 31 days, but the distribution is heavily right-skewed (mean 100 days) — a small number of complex projects take years, dragging down average performance metrics.
  • Geographic inequity is severe: the slowest ward (median 820 days) processes permits 68x slower than the fastest ward (median 12 days), even after filtering to wards with 200+ permits for statistical reliability.
  • Median processing time rose from ~28 days (2010-2018) to ~46-49 days (2021-2023), coinciding with the volume surge, before easing slightly to 34 days in 2025.
  • Permit type drives timeline more than anything else: New Building permits take a median of 276 days vs. 19 days for Small Residential Projects.

Business Context

A building permit is formal city approval to construct, demolish, renovate, or add to a property. Permits move through five stages: Application → Review → Issue → Inspection → Close. This dataset (Toronto Open Data, "Building Permits — Active Permits") is refreshed daily.

Who this matters to: city planning/operations staff, contractors and developers, real estate professionals, and residents.

Business Questions Answered

  1. Is permit demand growing? Yes — volume grew ~4x from 2010 to 2025.
  2. Which permit types take longest? New Building and New Houses permits take 4-9x longer than routine permits.
  3. Is there seasonality? Yes — applications peak in May, lowest in January (~35% swing).
  4. Which wards are underperforming? E2330, E2226, W0538 show 360-820 median days — a strong candidate for a staffing/process audit.
  5. Has service level improved or worsened? Worsened 2019-2023, early signs of improvement 2024-2025.

Data Quality Issues Found & How They Were Handled

IssueHandling
COMPLETED_DATE 100% nullDropped column
EST_CONST_COST stored as text with commas and a placeholder string instead of nullParsed to numeric, placeholder text converted to NaN
CURRENT_USE/PROPOSED_USE had 8,000-11,000+ inconsistent variantsNormalized via case-folding, whitespace/hyphen collapsing, explicit mapping
14 records with ISSUED_DATE before APPLICATION_DATEFlagged as anomalies, excluded from processing-time calculations
6 records with negative DWELLING_UNITS_CREATEDFlagged as anomalies
STATUS had 51 raw valuesGrouped into 6 categories
22,248 rows sharing a PERMIT_NUMConfirmed as legitimate permit revisions via REVISION_NUM, not duplicates

Recommendations

  1. Audit the slowest wards (E2330, E2226, W0538, N1629) for root cause.
  2. Set permit-type-specific SLAs rather than a single citywide target.
  3. Plan staffing for the May application surge.
  4. Investigate the 2021-2023 processing-time spike and whether the 2024-2025 improvement reflects a change worth formalizing.

Data Source

City of Toronto Open Data Portal — Building Permits: Active Permits, refreshed daily, published under the Open Government Licence – Toronto.

AI Research Assistant

Source: README.md, prnjl204/AI-Research-Assistant

A multi-agent research pipeline that takes a question, plans sub-questions, searches the web, cross-checks claims across sources for agreement or contradiction, and writes a structured, cited report — built entirely on free-tier tools (Groq's free API + DuckDuckGo search, no cost to run).

Why This Is Different From a Basic RAG Bot

Most "chat with search results" projects hand you an answer with no indication of how reliable it is. This one explicitly separates claims into:

  • Corroborated — 2+ independent sources agree
  • Contested — sources disagree (and the report says exactly how)
  • Unverified, single-source — only one source makes the claim

That verification step — not just retrieval — is the point of this project.

Architecture

Planner → Search → Verifier → Synthesizer
sub-questions   claims +        corroborated/     final report
                sources         contested/         (exec summary,
                                unverified          findings,
                                                     disagreements,
                                                     sources)

Built with LangGraph as an explicit state graph — each agent is a node, a single ResearchState Pydantic object is threaded through and updated at each step.

Setup (free, no credit card needed)

  1. Get a free Groq API key at console.groq.com
  2. Install dependencies: pip install -r requirements.txt
  3. Copy .env.example to .env and paste in your key
  4. Run: python main.py "your research question" or streamlit run app.py

Project Structure

ai-research-assistant/
├── schemas.py       # Pydantic models shared across all agents
├── llm.py           # Groq client wrapper (JSON-mode calls)
├── graph.py         # LangGraph wiring
├── main.py          # CLI test harness
├── app.py           # Streamlit UI with live agent progress
└── agents/
    ├── planner.py
    ├── search.py
    ├── verifier.py    # the key differentiator
    └── synthesizer.py

Notes on the Free-Tier Stack

  • LLM: Groq's free tier (Llama-class models) — fast enough that chaining 4 agent calls per run feels near-instant
  • Search: duckduckgo-search / ddgs, no API key required

Roadmap

  • Parallelize the search node across sub-questions
  • Add a confidence-score summary metric
  • Let users constrain sources (e.g. academic/government only)
  • PDF export of the final report

MedFlow Analytics

AI-Powered Healthcare Supply Chain Intelligence Platform

Source: README.md

A portfolio analytics project simulating a Data Analyst / Business Analyst / Process Improvement Consultant engagement at a regional healthcare product distributor — built end-to-end: synthetic data generation, SQL data modeling, predictive ML, supplier risk scoring, a BI dashboard, an LLM-powered insights assistant, and a Lean Six Sigma case study.

The Problem

MedFlow Distribution (fictional) supplies medical products to 80 hospitals/clinics via 15 suppliers, and is losing an estimated $2.3M annually to stockouts of critical supplies, expired inventory write-offs, and unreliable supplier delivery — discovered reactively, after the fact, through manual Excel reporting.

This project builds the system a lean ops team would actually use to catch these problems early: predictive risk models, a supplier accountability scorecard, and an AI assistant that surfaces what needs attention before it becomes a crisis.

What Makes This Different From a Typical Portfolio Dashboard

Most portfolio supply-chain projects are a single Power BI dashboard over a static CSV. This one is a full analytics pipeline:

  • Synthetic data generated with intentional, realistic patterns — not random noise. A supplier's performance genuinely deteriorates over 24 months in the data; that same deterioration is what the risk model catches and what the DMAIC case study investigates.
  • Two predictive models + one risk-scoring model + one rule-based risk model + one OR-based optimization model — not just visualizations.
  • A working AI assistant (real API-backed script) that answers natural-language questions grounded in the actual data, and explicitly declines to answer when the data doesn't support it.
  • An honest limitations section — this project states clearly where synthetic data makes results look better than real-world data would, rather than overselling model performance.

Key Findings

FindingNumber
Perishable inventory at risk of expiry write-off$18.3M (319 batches)
Suppliers in Red risk tier3 of 15
Worst supplier's on-time rate46.8% → 0%, sustained for 18 months
Worst supplier's average delay growth1.6 → 32.5 days over 24 months
Stockout early-warning model recall96% (ROC-AUC 0.996)
Reorder points needing recalibration1,284 of 1,560 SKU/hospital combos
Estimated excess carrying cost from miscalibrated stock$1.81M/year

Architecture

Synthetic Data Generator ──▶ SQLite DB (star schema, 10 tables) ──▶ Python ML Models
 (seeded patterns)                                                   (stockout, forecast,
                                                                       supplier risk,
                                                                       expiry risk,
                                                                       inventory optimization)
                                        │                                    │
                                        ▼                                    ▼
                          Power BI Dashboard (5 pages, DAX)      AI Insights Assistant
                          + optional web dashboard                (Anthropic API,
                                                                     NL Q&A + narrative)
                                        │
                                        ▼
                          DMAIC / A3 Case Study (Lean Six Sigma
                          root-cause analysis on supplier S013)

Tech Stack

  • Data: Python (pandas, numpy), SQLite, SQL
  • ML/Analytics: scikit-learn (HistGradientBoosting), engineered time-series features
  • BI: Power BI (DAX measures + build guide) and/or a custom web dashboard (React/Tailwind)
  • AI: Anthropic API for natural-language insights and Q&A
  • Process improvement: DMAIC / A3 methodology

Campaign Performance Investigator

Source: README.md

An agent that investigates why a marketing campaign is underperforming — not a chatbot, not a dashboard. Given a campaign that's over its target CPA, it plans an investigation, queries the data itself, adapts its approach when an initial query is inconclusive, validates its own conclusion, and hands a marketing analyst an evidence-backed hypothesis to approve — it never changes spend, pauses a campaign, or contacts anyone on its own.

Built as a portfolio project to demonstrate agentic AI system design for Data Analyst / AI Engineer roles: multi-step planning, tool selection, self-validation, vector memory (RAG), structured logging, and a real evaluation suite with a measured accuracy result.

The Problem It Solves

Marketing/analytics teams routinely burn analyst hours manually drilling into "why did this campaign underperform" — checking device breakdowns, geo breakdowns, time trends, one query at a time. This agent automates the investigation, not the decision: it does the tedious multi-step SQL digging and hands a human a ranked hypothesis with evidence, so the analyst's time goes to judgment, not query-writing.

Architecture

Underperforming campaign flagged
        │
        ▼
Agent: check device breakdown ──▶ Outlier found? ──No (inconclusive)──▶ Narrow time window, retry
        │                              │
        │                             Yes
        │                              ▼
        │                    Drill into WHEN the drop started
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        │                    Validate: other segments still healthy?
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        │                    Check vector memory: similar past cases?
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        │                    Form hypothesis + confidence score
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        │                    Save to investigations table
        │                              │
        │                              ▼
        └───────────────▶  Human review: Approve / Reject (no automatic action)

What Makes This Genuinely Agentic (Not Just a Script)

  • Plans multi-step: decides which dimension to check first, and whether to keep digging based on what it finds
  • Adapts to inconclusive results: when a full-range average hides an anomaly, it narrows the time window and retries — this exact gap was found and fixed via the evaluation suite
  • Chooses between tools: device breakdown, geo breakdown, time trend, and vector memory search — which ones get used depends on what earlier steps found
  • Validates its own conclusion before finalizing, rather than reporting the first pattern it notices
  • Uses memory: retrieves similar past investigations via a vector store
  • Human-in-the-loop by design: the agent's only possible outputs are a report and a database write to its own findings table — no code path can change a campaign, spend, or notify anyone

Tech Stack

LayerTechnologyWhy
DataSQLiteReal multi-table relational data — campaigns, daily metrics, investigations, audit trail, embeddings
Agent orchestrationHand-rolled Python state machineImplements plan/act/observe/adapt directly; a real Gemini function-calling version is also included
LLM integrationGoogle Gemini API, function callingReal model-driven investigation instead of fixed rules
Memory / RAGTF-IDF + cosine similarityFully local, zero-dependency vector search
DashboardStreamlitShows the live investigation trace + human approval flow
ObservabilityStructured JSON loggingEvery SQL query timed and logged, separate from the audit trail
DeploymentDocker + docker-composeSelf-seeding container, persistent named volume
EvaluationCustom eval harness8 synthetic ground-truth scenarios, scored for accuracy and false positive rate

Evaluation Results

100% dimension accuracy, 100% exact-value accuracy, 0 false positives, 0 false negatives across 8 synthetic ground-truth scenarios (device and geo anomalies of varying severity, plus healthy controls).

The first run scored 75% — the bug that caused it, the fix, and known limitations are documented in eval/EVALUATION_REPORT.md, a real gap found by testing rather than a polished final number.

The Gemini-driven agent has also been run end-to-end: given a campaign flagged as over target CPA, it independently planned and executed an 8-step investigation before producing a hypothesis — a mobile-specific conversion-rate collapse (from ~6.0% to ~1.0%) starting on a specific date, with desktop and tablet staying stable — returned with a 0.98 confidence score and supporting evidence matching the anomaly planted in the seed data.

Project Structure

campaign-investigator/
├── src/
│   ├── schema.sql                  # 5-table schema
│   ├── generate_seed_data.py       # synthetic demo data w/ planted anomaly

│   ├── agent.py                    # deterministic investigation loop
│   ├── agent_gemini.py             # real Gemini function-calling version
│   ├── persistence.py              # saves/loads investigations + human review
│   ├── memory.py                   # vector memory / RAG over past investigations
│   ├── observability.py            # structured JSON logging
│   └── dashboard.py                # Streamlit UI
├── eval/

python src/generate_seed_data.py
streamlit run src/dashboard.py
